messages:
liam: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression in nightly after the batch-selector tweak. Perfetto trace shows a tight loop of fused_flash_attn_kernel launches interleaved with kvcache_write kernels that look serialized. Sharing trace dump below.

anya: Can you paste the perfetto slice / link? quick note: the regression spikes at ~QPS 300 and seq_len ~384-512.

liam: perfetto trace excerpt:
```
Trace timeline (perfetto):
0.000s fused_flash_attn_kernel (SMs 56/80) 2.1ms
0.003s kvcache_write_kernel              0.45ms  <-- repeated bursts
0.004s memcpy_h2d_async                 0.12ms blocking on subsequent kernels
0.005s fused_flash_attn_kernel          6.8ms (stalls)
0.012s kvcache_write_kernel              3.2ms
```
Full trace: https://perfetto.local/trace/abcd1234 (internal)

sophia: nsys summary aligns: fused_flash_attn kernel P99 went from 2.2ms -> 7.0ms after the selector change. kvcache_write median ~0.4ms -> 2.9ms. Device timeline shows SMs spinning waiting on global memory store bandwidth; occupancy looks fine but L2/DRAM bandwidth saturates during bursts.

raj: Selector change notes: we started preferring fused variant when measured throughput > threshold for seq>=256. Looks like fused variant increases number of KV writes per token (coalescing changed), so write pressure jumps and causes serialization. Possible bank/stride aliasing? Also check that packed write code path didn't fall back to single-thread writes.

perf-bot: deploy-bot: canary reverted to commit c3f2a9b (batch-selector revert) at 2026-03-17T14:05Z :white_check_mark:

anya: Quick mitigation idea — tweak selector heuristic to prefer non-fused flash when kv_write_ratio > 0.15 or when observed memcpy stalls exceed X. Proposed patch snippet:
```
// heuristic in batch_selector.cpp
if (kv_write_ratio > 0.15 && avg_seq >= 256) {
  prefer_variant = Variant::FLASH_NONFUSED;
}
```
Would avoid the fused path when writes dominate.

sophia: From perfetto flame there are repeated write bursts aligned with our KV flush interval (every 64 tokens). That causes all concurrent batches to hit DRAM at same time -> IO storm. Two mitigations: (1) jitter flush timing across batches, (2) coalesce kvcache_write into a single batched write kernel that does lane-level aggregation to reduce outstanding stores.

liam: Action items: 1) keep canary reverted (done), 2) add kv_write_ratio instrumentation to batch metrics + endpoint to expose selector decision, 3) run nsys with per-warp counters and nvbit to capture memory op mix (INF-3219), 4) prototype coalesced kvcache_write kernel and benchmark (INF-3220). I'll own INF-3219/3220.

anya: I'll open a small PR to add the heuristic guard and flag the canary. Will add perf tests for seq 256/384/512 workloads.

raj: Also worth running a micro-benchmark to reproduce bank-stride aliasing: use varying lane writes and measure DRAM throughput. I can spin that up if you want.

liam: Yes please — raj, assign the microbench to yourself. I'll schedule an nsys run on the canary infra after PR lands. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
